text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Communist Akel party prefers former foreign minister George Iakovou to be the opposition candidate in next year's presidential poll.
- Parliament does not dare take a stand on the decriminalisation of homosexuality.
- A sacked pathologist is to sue the government for not paying him.
- Anti-gay protesters were foiled again because the issue was not on parliament's agenda yesterday.
- Cyprus Airways pilots start talks with company management on labour disputes.
- The agricultural insurance organisation, OGA, is on the brink of going bust. It has to pay 17 million pounds ($33.5 million) in compensation to farmers, but has only six million pounds in reserve.
- Akel counter-proposes George Iakovou to socialist Edek's proposal to field Greek deputy foreign minister Yannos Kranidiotis (a Cypriot) as the opposition's candidate in the presidential poll.
- United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan has prepared the invitations to Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots for direct talks.
- Everyone fears the cost of decriminalising homosexuality -- parliamentarians especially.
